question:
A 81-year-old male farmer presents with a neck mass. He has avoided medical care for over three
decades. His history includes smoking two packs of cigarettes daily since age 14 and weekly
consumption of a six-pack of beer. The physical exam reveals poor dental health, multiple actinic
keratoses, bilateral expiratory wheezes at the lung bases, and a 2.5-cm fixed, indurated mass on the
right side of his neck. No supraclavicular lymph nodes are detected. Flexible laryngoscopy shows no
abnormalities. His chest X-ray appears normal. Neck CT imaging reveals a 3-cm necrotic lymph node
and several smaller nodes on the right side, with no other significant findings. A cervical lymph node
biopsy confirms poorly differentiated squamous-cell carcinoma. Which of the following diagnostic
procedures is essential for the workup? Answer Choices: (A) MRI of the brain (B) Fine needle
aspiration of contralateral lymph nodes (C) Endoscopic examination of the upper esophagus (D)
Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy (E) CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis (F) Direct
laryngoscopy under anesthesia and concurrent tonsillectomy (G) PET-CT scan of head and neck (H)
Contrast-enhanced CT of brain and orbits (I) MRI of the nasopharynx and skull base (J)
Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of primary site
 A. Endoscopic examination of the upper esophagus
B. MRI of the brain
C. CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
D. Contrast-enhanced CT of brain and orbits
E. MRI of the nasopharynx and skull base
F. Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of primary site
G. Direct laryngoscopy under anesthesia and concurrent tonsillectomy
H. Fine needle aspiration of contralateral lymph nodes
I. PET-CT scan of head and neck
J. Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy
